segments.text: Morning Thabo, morning Lerato. Thanks for making time for the annual review.
Morning Sipho. Ja, a lot has changed since last year, so the timing is good.
Let's start with income. Thabo, last time you were on a hundred thousand a month gross.
That was before the promotion. It's one eighteen now, one hundred and eighteen thousand gross a month, from September.
Congratulations. And Lerato, are you still at Brightwater?
Still there. I take home forty-two thousand a month, same as last year.
And the bonus, Thabo?
The bonus is about a hundred and twenty, give or take, depending on how the year goes.
Let's talk about retirement. Last time we planned on sixty-five for you, Thabo.
Honestly, somewhere between sixty and sixty-five. Probably sixty-two, if the numbers allow it.
Most people in your position plan on about seventy percent of salary in retirement. Shall we use that?
If you say so. I haven't really thought about it.
Now the children. Neo is still at the independent school?
Yes, and the fees went up. It's about a hundred and five thousand for the year now.
And we're thinking of moving Kagiso to the same school next year.
She might study overseas one day. My sister's kids all went to the UK.
If she studies here it's about a hundred and fifty a year, but over there it's more like four-fifty.
Understood. Let's look at your retirement savings. Thabo, what is the retirement annuity on now?
The RA is sitting at about three-fifty, I think.
No, it's more like two-eighty. I saw the statement last month.
We'll check the statement. And how much is still owing on the bond?
We still owe about eighteen fifty on the bond.
Oh, and I took out disability cover through work in August. I don't know the amount yet.
No problem, we'll get the benefit schedule from HR. Any other investments since we last met?
I bought a few Krugerrands. They're in the safe at home, maybe sixty thousand worth.
Good to know. Lerato, last time you said you don't have a will.
We signed new wills in June, both of us, with the attorney.
That's a big one done. Did you name a guardian for the children?
Yes, my sister Palesa.
And groceries, still about nine thousand a month?
More like eleven now, with the prices.
And we still give my mom three and a half thousand a month, same as before.
Last thing: are you both still non-smokers?
Ja, neither of us smokes.
Great. I'll send a summary and a few questions to close the gaps.
